findings.proposedIrEvidence: ir-rule:170e314ceb35e54072b7ddba.exceptions[0..9] link only to permission rules for §6.01(a)(1)-(3) and §6.01(b)(1)(X),(1)(Y),(1)(Z),(3),(4)(a),(4)(b),(4)(c)
findings.verifierReasoning: The proposed IR models §6.01(a) as a single PROHIBITION rule whose 'exceptions' array is the mechanism connecting the blanket ban to the carve-outs that lift it. The source's own chapeau text states unambiguously that 'the provisions of Section 6.01(a) hereof shall not apply to' all 33 numbered clauses in (b). The proposed IR's exceptions array covers only roughly 10 of these carve-outs (through clause (4)(c)) and never links the prohibition to the ~20+ separately-modeled PERMISSION rules for clauses (5) through (33) (e.g. ir-rule:4b390b44... for (5)(a), ir-rule:8f3b7f1b... for (18)(i), ir-rule:2142a4b8... for (31), ir-rule:c2602aec... for (33), etc.), even though those rules exist elsewhere in the same IR as standalone permission objects. A consumer that relies on the prohibition rule's exceptions array to enumerate what actually carves out of the ban (a natural and common way to query 'what is this prohibition subject to') would conclude that only a small fraction of the source's actual permitted-debt universe exists, materially understating available capacity/permitted categories. The rule's own sufficiency is marked PARTIAL, but that flag does not convey the scale of the gap (roughly 70% of statutory carve-outs unlinked).
